info.title: Assure check answer
info.description: Focused description of the check answer: POST /v1/checks and GET /v1/checks/{check_id}, and the profile listing they take their profile ids and file names from, GET /v1/profiles (issue #2072), and the free pre-flight POST /v1/lint. The verdict's own fields are described in VERDICTS.md; this contract names the envelope and the optional upgrade object a free account's answer can carry.

post.description: Submit collected files for one profile (QUICKSTART-API.md, section 4). 200 with the verdict when the check finishes within 20 seconds of the request (its upload and admission included; an admission past 19.5 seconds leaves the check half a second), else 202 with the check id to poll.

get.description: The verdict of one of your checks, readable for 30 days; 202 while it runs.

parameters.name: request_bytes
parameters.description: The size pre-check (QUICKSTART-API.md, section 7): the byte count of the encoded body you are about to send to POST /v1/checks or POST /v1/declaration-proposal. Over your plan's limit the answer is the oversize_input refusal (413) that body would get, before any of it is sent; within it, the listing.

get.description: The served profiles, each with its input allow-list, byte caps and fail_on words, plus the global limits, the engine that answers, the planned profiles not served and the route table (QUICKSTART-API.md, section 6, the GET /v1/profiles row). Free.

post.description: The free pre-flight of an upload (QUICKSTART-API.md, section 6, the POST /v1/lint row): the body of POST /v1/checks, with the same optional fail_on and allow_partial query. It runs the checks that come before a check is admitted and answers 200 with the lint record; each problem lint finds in the upload is a finding in that record. It never runs a check, a model or a provider and is never charged. A body over the size limit is oversize_input (413) and a missing key is 401.

parameters.name: fail_on
parameters.description: As for POST /v1/checks: one of the words fail_on.accepted lists for the profile (GET /v1/profiles).

requestBody.description: The body of POST /v1/checks (QUICKSTART-API.md, section 4): the profile id, the collected files and, for a profile whose scope you select, scope and scope_binding.

Verdict.description: The verdict envelope (VERDICTS.md). Fields not listed here are described there.

charged.description: The check accounting flag on newly written server answers. Historical stored answers may omit it; a read-back preserves their bytes.

not_established.description: One entry per obligation not established (VERDICTS.md section 9).

because.description: Issue #1813, on postgresql-observed-baseline and python-auth-declared-model: which input sent the entry here. gate machine: the machine was refused or not read (premise the refusal reason, source the raw file it names); gate reading: the reading was not established (premise the declaration field or unobserved premise, an informational premise skipped, source raw/declaration.json#<field> or the raw file). A part nothing names is null.

Upgrade.description: Present only when the account is on the free plan and the server has a Premium payment link, or when a gifted plan ends within 30 days and the server has that link. Absent on every other paid plan; its presence changes no other field. The Action prints it as the first line of the job summary.

url.description: The Premium Stripe Payment Link with your account id, URL-encoded, as client_reference_id

line.description: One plain sentence that ends with url

notice.description: Present only when the free plan's USD 1 balance, shared by reports and requirement compiling, is spent, or when a gifted plan ends within 30 days ("Your gifted Premium plan ends on <date>.", and line is "To keep it, upgrade at <url>"): one plain sentence, printed at the start of the upgrade line

example.line: The proof tree for this run is on Assure Premium. Upgrade for USD 20 a month to see it: https://buy.stripe.com/<link id>?client_reference_id=gh-acme

charged.description: The check accounting flag on newly written server answers. Historical stored answers may omit it; a read-back preserves their bytes.

upgrade.description: Issue #4577: present only on a free account's allowance_exhausted refusal with detail.rule once_balance (a quote past what is left of its free USD 1) when the server has a Premium payment link, with notice when detail.allowance_remaining is 0 or less; the Action prints it in the job summary and the pull request comment.

request_id.description: The X-Request-Id of the request, on a refusal answered before a check was admitted (check_id null; issue #1101); absent when the envelope names a check_id.

served_from.description: Where the API served this failure from (issue #1665): handler when minted while answering this request, store when it is the admitted check's stored failure, first answered or read back.

build.description: Issue #1100: every freshly API-built refusal carries the serving engine's identity, including checker_error that refuses a development verdict; never copy the refused development block, kind or tree_sha256. Exactly commit, release_sha256 and checkers_sha256, the three keys of a verdict's engine block; all three are null if the engine pin fails verification. Compare build.commit first. Historical stored and non-API failures can omit this optional outer property and remain as originally written.

ProfileListing.description: The GET /v1/profiles answer (serve/api.py public_profiles). Keys not listed here may be added; none listed is removed.

build.description: Issue #1100: the top-level serving engine identity, exactly commit, release_sha256 and checkers_sha256, the three keys of a verdict's engine block. Compare build.commit first to distinguish a deploy lag from a changed answer. All three values are null if the engine pin cannot be verified; no kind or tree_sha256 is served here. This block is beside profiles and limits and changes no profile row.

body_bytes.description: The encoded request body your plan reads on POST /v1/checks and POST /v1/lint: Free 6 MiB, Premium 24 MiB, Pro 64 MiB.

engine.description: {commit, release}: the build that answers; both null while /healthz answers 503 engine_digest_mismatch.

not_served.description: [{id, stack, waits_on}]: the planned profiles this server knows about and does not serve.

routes.description: [{template, methods, free, rate_window, reads}]: the route table this server matches.

image.description: {files, manifest_sha256} of the built tree the server runs from, or null in a checkout.

served.description: Bounded possible statuses per obligation, keyed by served profile id. Obligations follow the profile order and reachable statuses follow its precedence order. Profiles without computable obligations are omitted.

plan.description: The account's plan and the request body it reads (the Director, 19 Oct 2026: Free 6 MiB, Premium 24 MiB, Pro 64 MiB); input_bytes equals limits.body_bytes.

ProfileRow.description: One served profile. The postgresql-declared-model row is pinned byte for byte (DIGEST-BASE) and carries stacks (issue #2650) but none of readings_shape, profile_sha256, collector, checker or docs. Keys not listed here may be added.

inputs.description: required: [{path, max_bytes}]; optional: [{path or pattern, max_bytes}]. A pattern must match the whole name.

excluded_by_design.description: The statuses the profile can emit that not_collected leaves out by design (needs_intent); absent from the postgresql-declared-model row.

fail_on.description: The words ?fail_on= takes for this profile, the default, the statuses not collected and the statuses excluded by design.

bias_default.description: refute or prove, or null when the checker declares no bias classes.

progress_notes.description: No served derive emits one; the 202 poll is the signal.

description.description: The profile's words, when the row has them.

requirement_states.description: mysql-declared-model only: the states each obligation can take.

scope.description: {max_ids, binding[, records]}: only for a profile whose scope you select.

stacks.description: The identity stacks the registry wires to the profile's checker (for python-auth-declared-model also to the python/fastapi, python/django (issue #266) and python/stdlib-http (issue #3840) adapters its free route runs; for a checker that runs a shared identity adapter as its leg, that adapter's row, issue #3495), or the database/endpoint kind (database/postgresql, database/mysql, endpoint/http) for the PostgreSQL, MySQL and HTTP profiles; on every row, the pinned one included (issue #2650). null for a registry-wired row when the server holds no readable adapter registry.

readings_shape.description: How scope_binding is sent; absent from the pinned row.

profile_sha256.description: The sha256 of the profile row file's bytes: the same digest a verdict for this profile carries as profile_sha256 (issue #2072). Absent from the pinned row.

collector.description: The registered collector claim: pinned, none or malformed, with its file when known. Absent from the pinned PostgreSQL row.

checker.description: The checker registry id, package and server derive path. Absent from the pinned PostgreSQL row.

docs.description: The quick-start section named by the profile row, when present. Absent from the pinned PostgreSQL row.

LintRecord.description: The lint record: every problem lint can find before a paid check, so all can be fixed first. ok true is not a clean bill: stages, stages_run, stages_skipped and not_checked say what ran and what was not checked.

ok.description: True when the record holds no finding (a notice included).

profile.description: The profile id linted; null when the body names no known profile.

findings.description: One object per problem, an unknown profile first, then in stage order. Each carries stage, outcome, severity (refusal or notice), a predicted charged, kind and text, and file, line or field where located.

requirements.description: requirements.md read row by row; null when no profile or no requirements text could be read.

matching.description: Present when the checker publishes no obligation statements or they could not be read; begins "none:".

would_run.description: True when no finding is a refusal, so the same body would run to a result.

would_charge.description: True when the same body would run, or would be refused by the checker once started.

stages.description: Each of the nine stages with its state.

not_checked.description: The admission checks this lint did not perform.

inputs_judged.description: The profile inputs the checker readers judged; null when the readers did not run.

build.description: The serving engine: compare build.commit first between answers; all null while the engine pin fails.

request_id.description: The X-Request-Id of this answer, the citation for a free lint (a lint has no check_id).
